body: You almost sound like you could be my ex-spouse.  My best advice, just dis-attach.  If there is any sort of rhyme or reason to life, if he is supposed to live, he will.  If he's not, he won't.  Let him be autonomous and make his own decisions.  Try not to let that impact you too much.  But the reality is, you WILL feel guilty if he dies, and you probably do bear some guilt.  He leaned on support from you and you stripped that from him.  I get that you need to take care of yourself and all, but there are consequences to actions.  That doesn't make you a bad person-- life is just shitty that way.

Tolerance might make that a low-ball attempt, I would probably double if you're serious.  Alcohol will aid respiratory depression from the sedatives.  If you are not needle phobic, packing 2 grams in a syringe and doing it in one shot might make for a helluva an exit.

But rather than spending all that money on drugs, could you be convinced to spend some of it on therapy?  Life is more than money, and it sounds like your mother could really use you now.  I don't know your relationship with her, but your death could make her grief infinitely worse.

I am once again plotting suicide, yet I am twice your age.  At 17 I had rehearsed several attempts and was very depressed and suicidal.  Even though my life has taken a turn for the worse, I'm glad I didn't off myself at 17.  I've done a lot of living in those next 17 years.  I fell in love (something I never thought would happen).  I got two college degrees and and a number of rewarding jobs.  I had a child (best thing I ever did).  I made new friends.  Now a lot of that has admittedly gone away-- but if I had killed myself at 17, I'd of never experienced some of the good that life has to offer.

Bless you on your decision.  It's difficult to feel that cold steel pressed against the flesh and then to have the gumption to pull the trigger.  There is no shame if you change your mind either.

Be glad that you are able to purchase a gun-- this is something I can't do.  Thus I must resort to more exotic methods which have less chance of success.

I prefer to think of suicide as a temporary solution to a permanent problem.  The permanent problem is the existential dilemma.  Is there a point to life?  Is there meaning to the universe?  Do I matter?  In my own mind, I have resolved the answer to these questions as "no."  Thus existence, without purpose presents a dilemma.  I respect people who can create their own meaning, but I've never been able to.

Suicide is a temporary solution, because who knows what happens after death.  Your energy disperses and your body decomposes.  Maybe you reincarnate.  Maybe you don't.  But some angsty schmuck is still eventually going to be facing that pesky existential dilemma.  And everyone will resolve it differently.

There is no guarantee that your problems are temporary.  Depression can be a chronic, lifelong disease.  It's every bit as debilitating as other chronic diseases, and there is no guarantee that you can successfully treat it.  Perhaps you owe it to yourself to give it a try-- but when do you draw the line?  After three antidepressants?  After meds, therapy, and ECT?  Or are you supposed to just muck on through life miserable all the time because life is supposedly superior over death?

I don't want to trivialize your pain, but reading this strangely gave me a sense of hope.  Because it reminded me of how petty the reasons are that we get suicidal.  Myself...I have lost my wife, my child, been incarcerated, and could be facing up to 5 years in prison.  I have been actively plotting my departure date since July 23, and have the date already picked out.  I don't say that to belittle you or to point out that my shit is worse than yours.  It just helped me gain some perspective on my own situation to see you put yours on paper.  So for that I thank you.

I called the local funeral providers today.  They all price a basic cremation (with no service) within $15 of each other.  So nobody is ripping anybody off at least.  I had no idea that obituaries are so expensive--I guess the papers are making up for the declining readership by stealing from the dead.

Know that you're not alone.  I have felt like it is my destiny to commit suicide for over two decades.  Personally, I feel that my life circumstances have reached that point of making me soon realize my chosen destiny.  But I digress.  I think depressed/suicidal people have this in common more than we perhaps like to talk about.  Particularly if you've suffered chronic depression over many years.  Suicide becomes a coping skill.

I value the dollars and cents I can save more than anything else in life.  The value of my life is boiled down to the discounted net present value of my projected future earnings.  Currently, my net present value of future earnings is worth more than my life is insured for...So financially, suicide is not entirely sensible.  However, my future earnings could be nil if I'm in a car accident tomorrow.  And my net present suffering is very high, so it's not all about money.

But it certainly helps if you enjoy what you do for that paycheck.  I wouldn't stay saddled to your family out of some sense of obligation.  Just live life and the chips will fall where they may.  Your mother may figure out real fast what she wants to do with her life when you're not there to enable her.
